Senators call tech CEOs to testify over AI license plate readers tracking citizens.
Evidence: Privacy concerns, State bans, Senate hearings
#Aletheia #Privacy #Tech 🌐

Lawmakers claim these congressional hearings protect citizen privacy and rein in unauthorized mass surveillance networks.
Stated Judgement: (+0.8, +0.5) — Greater Good

The hearings spotlight massive automated tracking without warrants, exposing deep regulatory gaps while state officials scramble for localized bans.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.6, -0.7) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: COND — The Path of Deception.
 Congressional scrutiny exposes invasive tracking, yet systemic reliance on surveillance for policing remains entirely intact.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 3.5, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Senate Inquiry: COND (0.5, 0.4) — Highlights privacy risks without halting expansion.
- Surveillance Tech: FAIL (-0.8, -0.9) — Normalizes continuous automated tracking.
Sen. Josh Hawley and fellow lawmakers have summoned the CEOs of Flock Safety and major tech rivals to testify regarding nationwide automated vehicle tracking networks.

The Bright Side:
High-profile congressional pushback forces secretive corporate data-sharing practices into public view.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing a procedural congressional investigation (WHAT) with an actual systemic legislative ban on warrantless mass tracking (WHO).

Social Physics Analysis:
Lawmakers run a procedural spectacle, staging hearings to project oversight while local police departments continue expanding automated dragnet contracts.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Systemic surveillance scales faster than committee warnings.

The Unavoidable Truth: Public oversight hearings reveal the staggering scale of warrantless civilian movement tracking.

The Unavoidable Lie: Congressional questioning alone will dismantle the multi-billion dollar municipal surveillance apparatus.
